title: SOLA: Optimizing SLO Attainment for Large Language Model Serving with State-Aware Scheduling
problem: Existing LLM serving systems apply coarse-grained, fixed scheduling policies (prefill-prioritized or decode-prioritized) that cause significant latency distribution bias between TTFT and TPOT and high inter-request variance, resulting in poor SLO attainment.
motivation: LLM serving SLOs specify both Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and Time-per-Output-Token (TPOT). Fixed scheduling strategies systematically over-satisfy one metric while violating the other. With vLLM's default strategy, 35% of requests fail TPOT SLOs even when their TTFT has substantial unused budget, indicating room for redistribution.
method: SOLA treats LLM request scheduling as a constrained optimization problem solved at each serving step, dynamically deciding which requests to serve, how many to bundle, and how many tokens to generate. Unlike systems with fixed priorities, SOLA continuously monitors actual performance—how long until the first response token arrives (TTFT) and how long between subsequent tokens (TPOT)—and picks the right strategy for each step: either minimize the longest gap between tokens while keeping first-token latency acceptable, or minimize the longest first-token latency while keeping between-token time acceptable. It executes this strategy through hierarchical prioritization (first among processing phases—prefill for input processing, decode for token generation—then among requests) using polynomial latency models that refine from real measurements, implemented in vLLM v0.4.2.
key_novelty: Rather than using fixed scheduling priorities, SOLA formulates LLM request scheduling as a constrained optimization problem that it solves fresh at each serving step, dynamically choosing whether to prioritize minimizing first-token latency or per-token latency based on real-time feedback about request states and system resources.
contributions: Formal design space for LLM scheduling: execution order (Fi), request count (ni), token count (ki)
State Monitor tracking per-request and system-level TTFT/TPOT state
Two constrained optimization problems capturing TTFT-TPOT trade-offs
Dynamic problem switching based on real-time SLO fulfillment ratios (pTTFT, pTPOT)
Hierarchical prioritization: phase-level then request-level sorting
Online polynomial cost model with iterative scaling ratio tuning
Peak memory prediction to avoid preemption overhead
SLO attainment improved from 45.5% to 99.4%; 1.04-1.27x more requests served

metrics.speedup: 1.04-1.27x more requests served than state-of-the-art at 90% SLO attainment; 1.04-1.11x at 99% attainment
metrics.accuracy: SLO attainment improved from 45.5% to 99.4% (Llama3-70B, ShareGPT, 4 A100s)
metrics.other: Scheduling overhead: 0.40-0.45% additional latency; evaluated on 8x A100 80GB SXM4

limitations: Evaluated only on co-located prefill+decode (not disaggregated systems)
Output length prediction accuracy affects scheduling quality
Scheduling overhead (0.40-0.45%) grows with system complexity
Cost model initialization requires offline profiling
SplitFuse chunk size sensitivity noted as a limitation of baseline comparison
